what_it_does: Cloud servers use SmartNICs — network interface cards with their own small processors — to offload the work of managing virtual network switches (software that routes packets between many virtual machines). These virtual switches look up each incoming packet in a table of flow rules to decide where to send it; as the number of tenants and rules grows, the SmartNIC's small fast memory (cache) fills up and misses, forcing slow lookups from the larger but slower main memory. Gigaflow observes that many packets pass through the same sequence of rule-table stages in order, so instead of caching only the final answer for a complete packet lookup, it caches the intermediate results partway through the table traversal. Because many different packets share those early stages, the intermediate results get reused far more often, dramatically improving cache hit rates even as the rule space grows large.
